title: Do waggle-dance angles follow the sun? An independent reanalysis

paper.citation: Dormagen DM, Wild B, Wario F, Landgraf T (2023) Machine learning reveals the waggle drift's role in the honey bee dance communication system. PNAS Nexus 2:pgad275. doi:10.1093/pnasnexus/pgad275

claims.claim: Foragers encode the direction of a food source relative to the sun's azimuth, so dances for a fixed feeder should rotate as the sun moves (von Frisch's classic finding).
claims.source: Background to the dataset; tested here on the deposited 2019 dances
claims.result: 793 dances (≥3 waggle runs, mean resultant length > 0.5) from 2 cameras and 2 feeders. In three of four camera–feeder groups the best-fitting slope of dance angle on sun azimuth was close to 1 (1.07, 0.53, 0.92, 1.11). Removing the sun's movement reduced the circular spread in every group. With the slope fixed at 1, the sun-corrected directions for the two feeders differ by 133.9° on camera 0 and 137.9° on camera 1, an agreement between independently recorded groups.
claims.scope: A minority of dances lie about 180° from the main cluster for their feeder, consistent with head–tail orientation errors in automatic tracking; they were kept, which widens the spread. Angles are in each camera's image frame; their sign and zero are not tied to gravity in the deposit, so only the rate of change is tested, not the absolute direction. Dances by the same bee are not independent; the bootstrap intervals resample dances and are therefore optimistic.

method: Waggle phases were assigned to a dance when they came from the same camera, fell between the dance's start and end times and lay within 60 px of its median position. Each dance angle is the circular mean of its waggle phases. Sun azimuth was computed with the NOAA solar-position equations at 52.456° N, 13.296° E (between the two feeders listed in the log; the hive coordinates are not given). For each camera and feeder the slope k in angle = c + k·azimuth was chosen by maximising the mean resultant length of the residuals over k ∈ [−2, 2]; 95% intervals from 300 bootstrap resamples of dances.
limits: A slope of +1 rather than −1 reflects the camera's image-coordinate convention. This is an exploratory reanalysis, not a reproduction of the paper's waggle-drift results.
